choices.text: Do the job anyway. The Pavilion does not pay for opinions

effects.log: You put the noodle money on the counter and go to work. Some nights you have to choose not to know things.

choices.text: Spare {him}, and leave the envelope where {he} will find it

effects.log: You walk past the gate twice and keep walking. It is the strangest thing you have ever done with a contract.

choices.text: Take the truth back to the client, with the silver

effects.log: You turn around on the road. The client is going to have a very surprising evening.

events.text: {npc} rides out to the county seat twice a month in a green sedan chair, with eight constables and a clerk who reads poetry aloud. The road narrows at a bamboo cutting where the chair has to slow.

choices.text: Come down on the guards from both sides of the road

ok.log: The guards break and scatter. Only one does not run, and steps into the road in front of {npc}.

fail.log: There are more guards than the scouts said, and they are better. You get away bleeding into the brush.
fail.deathCause: a Hushed Lantern contract that went wrong

choices.text: One arrow from the ridge, before anyone sees you

ok.log: One arrow, from very far away. By the time the guards look up, the ridge is empty and {npc} is not getting up.

fail.log: The wind takes it. The arrow buries itself in the sedan pole, and the whole road starts shouting at the ridge.

choices.text: Bring the hillside down behind them and cut them off

ok.log: Rocks fill the road behind the guards. In the dust and the shouting, the way to {npc} is open, except for one figure.

fail.log: The rocks come down too early and block the road in front of you instead. You climb out of the dust and go.

choices.text: Let the party pass. There will be another road

effects.log: You watch them go by below you, close enough to hit with a pebble. Another day.

events.text: For three months you are the new copyist at the yamen, under a borrowed name, with ink on your fingers. {npc} likes your hand, and asks for you to copy {his} private letters at night.

choices.text: Wait for the one night {he} trusts you completely

ok.log: On the night it happens, {npc} is laughing at something you said. Then {he} is not. You walk out through the front gate, bowing to the porter.

fail.log: Someone from your old life recognises your face in the market. By evening the household is looking for you, and the captain is at the inner door.

choices.text: A needle at the right point, while {he} is dressing

ok.log: One touch at the back of the neck, while you straighten a collar. {npc} sits down as if tired, and you go to fetch a physician who will be too late.

fail.log: Your hand hesitates at the collar and {npc} feels it. {He} looks at you in the mirror, and calls for the guard.

choices.text: Let them find you out, and take the captain first

ok.log: You leave a trail on purpose and wait where it leads. The captain comes alone, as captains do when they are proud.

fail.log: The trail you left is followed by twenty men, not one. You go over the roofs with nothing done.

choices.text: Give notice, and leave the household for good

effects.log: You hand in your apron and your borrowed name together. In the end, you liked the work.

events.text: At a ferry landing a young fighter steps off the boat and does not move out of your way. {npc}. You have heard the name before, at a funeral, years ago. "You killed my parent for silver," {he} says. "I have trained every day since."

ok.log: The sword spins away into the grass. {npc} waits for the blow, and it does not come.

events.text: Your face, badly drawn, is on the gate of every town in the province now, and the price under it has gone up. Three bounty hunters with a copy of it are waiting at the inn where you stop for the night.

choices.text: Fight your way through

ok.log: When it is over nobody else in the province is in a hurry to collect that price.

fail.log: They are better than the poster deserved. You get away with a bolt in the shoulder and the price still on your head.

choices.text: Pay them more than the bounty (300 taels)

effects.log: Silver solves most things. The hunters remember they were looking for someone taller.

choices.text: Lie low until it passes

ok.log: A month in a hayloft, and then a bigger crime somewhere else takes everyone's attention. You come down.

fail.log: The hayloft belongs to a farmer who can read. You leave in a hurry, in the rain.

events.text: After your third contract a blind old woman who sells lanterns stops you in the street and presses one into your hands. Inside the paper, where the candle goes, there is a crescent moon cut in black. "The Keeper of Lanterns says you are one of us now," she says. "Not everyone lasts three."

choices.text: Thank the Keeper, and ask what the moon means

effects.log: "It means nobody sees you coming," the old woman says, "and that you never see who sends you." She laughs at your face.

choices.text: Ask for a bigger share of the next fee

ok.log: The old woman laughs until she coughs, and puts 200 taels in your hand. "For nerve," she says.

fail.log: The old woman stops laughing. "Three is not thirty," she says, and walks away with her lanterns.

choices.text: Burn the lantern. You belong to no one

effects.log: You burn it in the gutter. Somewhere above you, on a roof, somebody writes that down too.

events.text: Ten contracts. The Pavilion sends someone to measure you: Night Blade Han, who has twenty, waits on your roof one night with two wooden swords. "The Keeper wants to know if you are luck or skill," Han says. "So do I."

choices.text: Cross wooden swords with Han

ok.log: Han's wooden sword clatters down into the courtyard. Han laughs and goes after it. "Skill," Han tells the Keeper.

fail.log: Han raps your knuckles, your elbow and the back of your head, gently, and then shows you how. You learn more in a night than in a year.

choices.text: Talk shop with Han until the sun comes up

effects.log: Han knows every rooftop of the capital and every guard captain's weakness, and tells you half of them.

choices.text: Tell Han to go home

effects.log: "Luck, then," Han says, and goes. The next envelope is slow to come, and very well paid.

events.text: The old Lord of the Hushed Lantern takes you to the top of the Pavilion, where nobody goes, and gives you the ledger: every name the Pavilion has ever taken, for three hundred years, in a small neat hand. "Now you write in it," the old Lord says. "And now you find out who reads it."

choices.text: Read the ledger from the first page

effects.log: It takes a month. By the end you know which emperors, which sects and which saints paid the Pavilion, and you will never be able to forget it.

choices.text: Ask who reads it

ok.log: The old Lord smiles for the first time. "Clever. Nobody. That is the point of it." You understand that the Pavilion answers to no one, now including you.

fail.log: The old Lord does not answer, and you never ask again.

choices.text: Close the ledger, and say nothing

effects.log: You close it on the old Lord's hands. Some books are better carried than read.
